🎬 Cadillac Records (2008)

Cadillac Records tells the extraordinary story of the rise of Chess Records, the legendary Chicago record label that helped transform American music during the 1950s and 1960s. The film follows ambitious record producer Leonard Chess as he builds a successful music empire by discovering and promoting some of the most influential blues and rock and roll artists of their generation. Beginning with the remarkable talent of Muddy Waters, Chess recognizes the growing popularity of electric blues and works to bring its powerful sound to audiences across the country. As the label expands, legendary performers including Little Walter, Howlin’ Wolf, Chuck Berry, and Etta James become part of its musical legacy, each bringing unique personalities, extraordinary talent, and complicated personal struggles. Behind the success of their groundbreaking recordings lies a world filled with racial discrimination, financial disagreements, romantic relationships, jealousy, addiction, and the pressures of fame. As Chess attempts to manage his growing business and the unpredictable lives of his artists, personal conflicts and changing musical trends threaten the stability of the label. Meanwhile, the musicians struggle to balance their artistic ambitions with the realities of an industry that does not always reward them fairly. Through unforgettable performances, emotional confrontations, and iconic musical moments, the film celebrates the artists whose creativity helped shape modern popular music. Combining powerful performances, historical drama, and legendary blues and rock and roll music, Cadillac Records explores ambition, friendship, betrayal, cultural influence, and the lasting legacy of American music.

🎭 Genre: Biography • Drama • Music

⭐ IMDb: 7.0/10

⏱️ Runtime: 1h 49m • R

🎥 Director: Darnell Martin

source_details.synopsis: Cadillac Records is a 2008 American biographical drama film written and directed by Darnell Martin. The film explores the musical era from the early 1940s to the late 1960s, chronicling the life of the influential Chicago-based record-company executive Leonard Chess, and a few of the musicians who recorded for Chess Records. The film stars Adrien Brody as Leonard Chess, Jeffrey Wright as Muddy Waters, Columbus Short as Little Walter, Cedric the Entertainer as Willie Dixon, Eamonn Walker as Howlin' Wolf, Mos Def as Chuck Berry, and Beyoncé Knowles as Etta James. The film was released in North America on December 5, 2008, by TriStar Pictures. The soundtrack was released on Music World/Columbia
